text: Trusted contracts' backing tests run in the gate, and support trusted assumptions without proving them (#350, #294's step 4). Each contract's declared invocations run like the application's other tests, offline in its admitted dependency image, keyed by the contract's declaration, and every backing test needs one or preflight refuses the manifest. Before its tests load, the runner resolves the operation to its real implementation: the application declaration in its staged source, a standard-library function or class from the runtime's own library or built in, or an installed distribution's code in the libraries directory whose file the distribution's RECORD lists. It counts each test's calls into that implementation and records each outermost unittest assertion and its outcome. A test supports its contract only when it passed, exercised, in a run that passed, with calls into an implementation the report binds: the declaration's own source, the bound wheel's name and version with a RECORD-listed file, or no distribution for the standard library. So a test that reached only a stub or substitute supports nothing, and a run of a test that failed, was skipped or reached no implementation vetoes another's pass. A contract whose backing tests ran without all supporting it gets an unsupported_contract diagnostic naming each test's shortfall, and the gate passes only when every declared contract is tested, used by a proof or not. Tested support makes no contract assumed, proved or a checked call boundary.
